classes.objetivo: Reconocer las partes de un informe sobre hábitos de sueño y el marcador que introduce cada una, con tono objetivo.

ensenanza.en: The aim of this report is to examine the sleep habits of secondary students, and the introduction must set out the scope of the study.
ensenanza.es: El objetivo de este informe es examinar los hábitos de sueño de los estudiantes de secundaria, y la introducción debe exponer el alcance del estudio.
ensenanza.nota: The aim of this report is to + verbo base es el marcador típico de la introducción; scope es lo que el estudio cubre y lo que no.

ensenanza.en: The method section explains how the researchers chose to carry out an online survey, in which every respondent answered ten questions.
ensenanza.es: La sección de método explica cómo decidieron los investigadores llevar a cabo una encuesta en línea, en la que cada encuestado respondió diez preguntas.
ensenanza.nota: Carry out es el verbo habitual para realizar una encuesta o un estudio; respondent es la persona que contesta una encuesta.

ensenanza.en: The main findings show that 62 percent of students sleep less than eight hours, and this section reports the data without any comment.
ensenanza.es: Los principales resultados muestran que el 62 % de los estudiantes duerme menos de ocho horas, y esta sección presenta los datos sin ningún comentario.
ensenanza.nota: Findings es plural: lleva show, no shows. Esta parte da los datos sin opinar.

ensenanza.en: The conclusion is that late screen use may affect sleep, although the sample is small and the report stays impartial about the cause.
ensenanza.es: La conclusión es que el uso de pantallas por la noche puede afectar al sueño, aunque la muestra es pequeña y el informe se mantiene imparcial sobre la causa.
ensenanza.nota: La conclusión interpreta los resultados con prudencia (may) y reconoce un límite; impartial = sin tomar partido.

ensenanza.en: The report makes one recommendation: schools should start classes a little later, and this advice follows directly from the findings.
ensenanza.es: El informe hace una recomendación: los colegios deberían empezar las clases un poco más tarde, y este consejo se deriva directamente de los resultados.
ensenanza.nota: La recomendación dice qué hacer a partir de la conclusión; suele llevar should o it is recommended that.

ensenanza.en: The summary at the start of a report gives a busy reader the aim, the key finding and the main recommendation in just four sentences.
ensenanza.es: El resumen al comienzo de un informe da a un lector ocupado el objetivo, el hallazgo clave y la recomendación principal en solo cuatro frases.
ensenanza.nota: Summary resume todo el informe y se escribe al final, aunque se coloque al principio.

explicacion.titulo: Las partes de un informe y sus marcadores
explicacion.texto: Un informe breve tiene partes fijas, y cada una se anuncia con un marcador: Summary (resume todo), Introduction: The aim of this report is to… (objetivo y alcance, scope), Method: The method was… o Data were collected… (cómo se llevó a cabo el estudio), Findings: The main findings show that… (qué salió), Conclusion y Recommendation: The conclusion is that… / It is recommended that… El tono es objetivo e impartial: sin I think, sin exclamaciones y sin lenguaje emocional. Se habla de datos, no de sentimientos.

patron.texto: Marcador de la sección + contenido neutro:

formula.texto: The aim of this report is to
examine students' sleep habits.
The main findings show that
formula.nota: resultados: lo que salió de los datos

formula.texto: It is recommended that

filas.texto: This report examines… The key finding is…
The aim of this report is to…
The method was… / Data were collected…

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: The aim of this report is examine the sleep of students.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: The aim of this report is to examine the sleep of students.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Después de The aim is va to + verbo base; en español «es examinar» no lleva nada, pero en inglés hace falta to.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: The main findings shows that 62 percent sleep little.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: The main findings show that 62 percent sleep little.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Findings es plural y el verbo debe concordar: show.

situacion.contexto: Sara ha escrito un informe sobre el sueño para la revista del colegio y Leo la ayuda a ordenarlo.

dialogo.texto: I've written a report on sleep habits, but the teacher says it is hard to follow.
dialogo.traduccion: He escrito un informe sobre hábitos de sueño, pero la profesora dice que es difícil de seguir.

dialogo.texto: Start with the aim: The aim of this report is to examine how much students sleep.
dialogo.traduccion: Empieza con el objetivo: El objetivo de este informe es examinar cuánto duermen los estudiantes.

dialogo.texto: Then the method: an online survey with 120 respondents.
dialogo.traduccion: Luego el método: una encuesta en línea con 120 encuestados.

dialogo.texto: Right. After that, the findings. Keep the tone neutral, so no «I think».
dialogo.traduccion: Correcto. Después, los resultados. Mantén el tono neutro, así que nada de «creo que».

dialogo.texto: And the conclusion and the recommendation go at the end.
dialogo.traduccion: Y la conclusión y la recomendación van al final.

item.consigna: ¿Qué orden de partes y qué tono propone Leo para el informe?

opciones.es: Objetivo, método, resultados, conclusión y recomendación, con tono neutro.
Objetivo, resultados, método, conclusión y recomendación, con tono neutro.
Objetivo, método, resultados, conclusión y recomendación, con tono personal.

item.feedback: Leo propone objetivo (aim), método, resultados (findings) y, al final, conclusión y recomendación, sin «I think».

guiada.consigna: Lee el fragmento y elige a qué sección del informe pertenece.
guiada.feedback: El fragmento cuenta cómo se recogieron los datos (en línea, en marzo, con diez preguntas): es la sección de método.
opciones: Method: it explains how the data were gathered.
Findings: it reports what the survey showed.
Introduction: it says why the report was written.
guiada.texto: Data were collected through an online survey in March. A total of 120 students answered ten questions about their sleep and their use of screens during the first week of the month.
guiada.pista: Fíjate en si el texto explica cómo se recogieron los datos o qué salió.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «El objetivo de este informe es examinar cuánto duermen los estudiantes.»
guiada.feedback: The aim of this report is to + verbo es el marcador clásico de una introducción: dice para qué se escribió el informe.
guiada.texto: Every report begins by saying why it was written. The ___ of this report is to examine how much sleep secondary students get, and the next section explains how the data were collected.
guiada.pista: Es el sustantivo que dice para qué se escribió el informe.

guiada.consigna: Ordena: «Los principales resultados muestran que el 62 % duerme menos de ocho horas.»
guiada.feedback: Findings es plural y lleva show; that introduce el dato principal de la sección de resultados.
guiada.respuesta: The main findings show that 62 percent sleep less than eight hours
guiada.pista: Empieza por el sujeto plural: los principales resultados.

practica.consigna: Escucha y elige en qué parte del informe se interpretan los datos.
practica.feedback: La presentadora dice que los resultados se presentan sin comentario y que solo la conclusión interpreta los datos.
practica.audio: Let me talk you through a typical short report. It begins with a summary, so that a busy reader can get the key point in seconds. Then the introduction sets out the aim and the scope. The method explains how the survey was carried out, and the findings present the data without comment. Only the conclusion interprets them, and the recommendation says what should happen next.
opciones: In the conclusion, after the findings have been presented.
In the recommendation, which explains what the data mean.
In the findings, where each figure is commented on.

practica.consigna: Relaciona cada marcador de un informe con la sección que introduce.
practica.feedback: Cada marcador anuncia una sección distinta del informe: objetivo, método, resultados y recomendación.
pares: The aim of this report is to…
Introducción: el objetivo del estudio
The method was an online survey.
Método: cómo se recogieron los datos
The main findings show that…
Resultados: qué salió de los datos
It is recommended that schools…
Recomendación: qué hay que hacer

practica.consigna: Mia edita una sección de resultados. Elige la frase que mantiene un tono objetivo.
practica.feedback: Un apartado de resultados da cifras y fuente; las otras frases añaden valoraciones personales (sadly, I believe).
opciones: The survey shows that 62 percent of respondents sleep fewer than eight hours.
Sadly, it is shocking that most students sleep so little, and schools must act.
I believe these findings prove that students are careless about their sleep habits.
practica.texto: Mia is editing the findings section of her report on sleep habits. The teacher has asked her to keep an impartial, neutral tone and to leave any personal comment out. She is choosing between three sentences for the first line.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha y elige qué opina la profesora del borrador en conjunto.
evaluacion.feedback: La profesora alaba la estructura y la recomendación, pero pide corregir dos puntos: falta el método y los resultados opinan.
evaluacion.audio: Thank you for sending your draft on student sleep. The structure is clear: you open with a summary and then state your aim. However, your method section is missing, so readers cannot tell how many students answered, or how the survey was carried out. Also, your findings section slips into opinion, with phrases like I think and sadly. A report should keep an impartial tone and save interpretation for the conclusion. Fix those two points, and the recommendation, which is already well written, will be much more convincing.
opciones: That it is promising, but two sections need to be revised.
That it is well written, but the survey should have been larger.
That it is nearly ready, since only the tone of the recommendation needs changing.

evaluacion.consigna: Con el mismo audio, elige por qué pide quitar «I think» y «sadly».
evaluacion.feedback: La profesora dice que el informe debe mantener un tono imparcial y dejar la interpretación para la conclusión.
evaluacion.audio: Thank you for sending your draft on student sleep. The structure is clear: you open with a summary and then state your aim. However, your method section is missing, so readers cannot tell how many students answered, or how the survey was carried out. Also, your findings section slips into opinion, with phrases like I think and sadly. A report should keep an impartial tone and save interpretation for the conclusion. Fix those two points, and the recommendation, which is already well written, will be much more convincing.
opciones: Because a findings section should stay impartial and leave interpretation for later.
Because those phrases are too informal for any part of a report.
Because they make the recommendation sound weaker than it is.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «120 encuestados completaron la encuesta; veinte dejaron preguntas en blanco.»
evaluacion.feedback: Respondents son las personas que contestan una encuesta; el informe indica cuántos fueron y cuántos dejaron respuestas vacías.
evaluacion.texto: A total of 120 ___ completed the survey, although twenty of them left several questions blank. The results below are based on the answers that were complete.

evaluacion.consigna: Lee las cuatro frases y elige el orden en que aparecen en un informe.
evaluacion.feedback: El orden habitual es objetivo (B), método (D), resultados (C) y recomendación al final (A).
opciones: B, D, C, A
B, C, D, A
D, B, C, A
evaluacion.texto: A: 'It is recommended that schools start classes later.' B: 'The aim of this report is to examine student sleep.' C: 'The main findings show that 62 percent sleep under eight hours.' D: 'Data were collected through an online survey of 120 students.'

repaso.consigna: Elige qué problema tiene este fragmento para un informe.
repaso.feedback: El fragmento da un dato (la mayoría revisa mensajes), pero lo adorna con juicios (regrettably, clearly unacceptable) impropios de un informe.
opciones: It mixes facts with personal judgement, which breaks a neutral tone.
It draws its conclusion before it has stated the aim of the study.
It is written in a tone that is too formal for a report.
repaso.texto: Extract from a draft: 'This report examines how students use their phones at night. Regrettably, most respondents admit that they check their messages after midnight, which is clearly unacceptable.'

repaso.consigna: Escucha y elige por qué la recomendación va al final del informe.
repaso.feedback: El hablante dice que la recomendación depende de la conclusión, por eso va después.
repaso.audio: Two students are planning their report. One of them says: Begin with the aim, then the method. Put the recommendation last, since it depends on the conclusion that comes before it. And remember that the findings are for facts: if you want to add a comment, wait until the conclusion.
opciones: Because it builds on the conclusion, which has to be reached first.
Because readers usually skip the last part of a report.
Because it summarises the findings for busy readers.

repaso.consigna: Completa: «El informe tenía cuarenta páginas, así que la directora leyó solo el resumen.»
repaso.feedback: El resumen condensa objetivo y resultado principal para quien no va a leer el informe completo.
repaso.texto: The report has forty pages, so the manager read only the ___ on the first page, which gave her the aim and the main result.

classes.objetivo: Matizar hallazgos rotundos con estructuras impersonales: there is some evidence that, it appears that, it remains unclear whether, to some extent.

ensenanza.en: It remains unclear whether the new timetable improves sleep, because the evidence so far is not conclusive and covers only one school.
ensenanza.es: Sigue sin estar claro si el nuevo horario mejora el sueño, porque las pruebas hasta ahora no son concluyentes y cubren un solo colegio.
ensenanza.nota: It remains unclear whether + cláusula: todavía no hay respuesta. Con la duda se usa whether, no that.

ensenanza.en: There is some tentative evidence that longer sleep improves concentration, but the studies are small, so a degree of caution is needed.
ensenanza.es: Hay algunas pruebas provisionales de que dormir más mejora la concentración, pero los estudios son pequeños, así que hace falta cierta cautela.
ensenanza.nota: There is some evidence that… admite que hay datos, pero débiles. Evidence es incontable: no lleva -s.

ensenanza.en: To a certain extent, the results are explained by the later start of lessons, although they are largely based on what students said.
ensenanza.es: Hasta cierto punto, los resultados se explican por el inicio más tardío de las clases, aunque se basan en gran medida en lo que dijeron los estudiantes.
ensenanza.nota: To a certain extent (o to some extent) limita el alcance de la afirmación; largely reduce la fuerza de la base de datos.

ensenanza.en: It appears that screen time affects sleep, but a small sample could easily call into question a result that looks convincing at first.
ensenanza.es: Parece que el tiempo de pantalla afecta al sueño, pero una muestra pequeña podría poner en duda fácilmente un resultado que al principio resulta convincente.
ensenanza.nota: It appears that… introduce una inferencia prudente; call into question significa poner en duda.

ensenanza.en: The data indicate that most students sleep too little, but the sample was somewhat small, so the authors ask readers to interpret it carefully.
ensenanza.es: Los datos indican que la mayoría de los estudiantes duerme muy poco, pero la muestra era algo pequeña, así que los autores piden a los lectores que la interpreten con cuidado.
ensenanza.nota: Indicate es más fuerte que appears; somewhat suaviza una crítica al método.

ensenanza.en: Headlines such as 'Screens ruin sleep' are much too strong, so a careful report turns them into statements that match the evidence.
ensenanza.es: Titulares como «Las pantallas arruinan el sueño» son demasiado fuertes, así que un informe cuidadoso los convierte en enunciados que se ajustan a las pruebas.
ensenanza.nota: Ruin es un verbo rotundo; el informe lo sustituye por estructuras matizadas como there is some evidence that…

explicacion.titulo: Matizar lo que dicen los datos
explicacion.texto: Un informe no afirma más de lo que los datos permiten. Por eso convierte frases rotundas («Screens ruin sleep») en frases matizadas con estructuras impersonales: There is some evidence that… (hay indicios), It appears that… (parece que), It remains unclear whether… (no está claro si) y To a certain extent… / To some extent… (hasta cierto punto). Tras unclear se usa whether, no that. Además, may, tend to, a degree of y adverbios como largely o somewhat bajan el grado de certeza, y not conclusive avisa de que los datos no bastan para cerrar el asunto.

formula.texto: It appears that
screen use
may affect sleep,
formula.nota: verbo con may: grado bajo de certeza

formula.texto: to some extent.

filas.texto: It appears that… / There is some evidence that…

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: It remains unclear that the later start improves sleep.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: It remains unclear whether the later start improves sleep.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Con unclear se expresa la duda con whether; that presentaría el dato como seguro.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: There are some evidences that screens affect sleep.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: There is some evidence that screens affect sleep.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Evidence es incontable: no tiene plural y va con is.

situacion.contexto: Ana enseña a Tom el borrador de su informe y Tom le sugiere suavizar una frase demasiado rotunda.

dialogo.texto: Your draft says: «Screens ruin students' sleep.» That sounds too strong.
dialogo.traduccion: Tu borrador dice: «Las pantallas arruinan el sueño de los estudiantes». Suena demasiado fuerte.

dialogo.texto: But many students said they sleep badly after using their phones.
dialogo.traduccion: Pero muchos estudiantes dijeron que duermen mal después de usar el móvil.

dialogo.texto: Yes, but the survey only shows an association. How about: There is some evidence that screens affect sleep?
dialogo.traduccion: Sí, pero la encuesta solo muestra una asociación. ¿Qué tal: Hay algunos indicios de que las pantallas afectan al sueño?

dialogo.texto: Better. And we don't know whether the effect is big. It remains unclear how big it is.
dialogo.traduccion: Mejor. Y no sabemos si el efecto es grande. Sigue sin estar claro cuánto es.

dialogo.texto: Exactly. A report should say what the data allow, not more.
dialogo.traduccion: Exacto. Un informe debe decir lo que permiten los datos, no más.

item.consigna: ¿Por qué Tom propone cambiar la frase de Ana?

opciones.es: Porque la encuesta solo muestra una asociación y la frase es demasiado rotunda.
Porque la frase no dice cuántos estudiantes respondieron a la encuesta.
Porque la encuesta demuestra que las pantallas no afectan al sueño.

item.feedback: Tom dice que la encuesta «only shows an association» y propone «There is some evidence that…», que admite que la evidencia es limitada.

guiada.consigna: Elige la reformulación que ajusta el grado de certeza a los datos de la encuesta.
guiada.feedback: La encuesta solo halló un vínculo en un colegio: There is some evidence that… y may admiten esa base débil sin afirmar una causa.
opciones: There is some evidence that late screen use may be linked to shorter sleep.
It is clear that late screen use is the reason why students sleep less.
It remains unclear whether late screen use has any link with how long students sleep.
guiada.texto: Draft finding: 'Late screen use ruins students' sleep.' However, the survey of 120 students only found that those who use screens late sleep less. It did not measure the reason, and it covered one school.
guiada.pista: El estudio solo halló un vínculo en un colegio: busca la estructura que admite una prueba débil.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «Aún no está claro si el nuevo horario mejora el sueño.»
guiada.feedback: Tras unclear se introduce la duda con whether (o if), no con that.
guiada.texto: The study has only just started and the first results are not yet available. It remains unclear ___ the new timetable improves sleep.
guiada.pista: Es la conjunción que introduce una duda entre dos posibilidades: sí o no.

guiada.consigna: Ordena: «Hasta cierto punto, los resultados se explican por el inicio más tardío.»
guiada.feedback: To a certain extent limita el alcance: el inicio más tardío explica solo una parte de los resultados.
guiada.respuesta: To a certain extent the results are explained by the later start
guiada.pista: Empieza por el matizador que significa «hasta cierto punto».

practica.consigna: Escucha y elige qué concluye la investigadora sobre el cambio de horario.
practica.feedback: La investigadora admite que solo hay indicios débiles y pide un estudio mayor antes de cambiar horarios.
practica.audio: A researcher is summing up her study for the school newspaper. There is some tentative evidence that students who start lessons later concentrate better, but she is careful. Only one school took part, and the survey was somewhat limited. It remains unclear whether the effect would last over a whole year. She therefore calls for a larger study before any school changes its timetable.
opciones: That more research is needed before schools change their timetables.
That later lessons improve concentration, so every school should start later.
That the effect has been confirmed in one school over a whole year.

practica.consigna: Reescribe con matiz: «Homework ruins students' free time.»
practica.feedback: La frase lleva There is some evidence that… más una segunda cautela (may, tends to, it remains unclear) y evita el verbo rotundo ruin.
practica.texto: Hallazgo rotundo: «Homework ruins students' free time.» Reescríbelo para un informe con There is some evidence that… y una segunda cautela (may, it remains unclear…).
practica.respuesta: There is some evidence that homework may reduce students' free time, although it remains unclear how much.
aceptadas: There is some evidence that homework can reduce students' free time, but it is unclear how large the effect is.
There is some evidence that homework tends to reduce students' free time, although the survey was somewhat limited.

practica.consigna: Relaciona cada frase del informe con el grado de certeza que expresa.
practica.feedback: Indicate es más fuerte que appears; it remains unclear marca duda abierta y to a certain extent limita el alcance.
pares: The data indicate that most students sleep too little.
Certeza alta: los datos lo señalan con fuerza
It appears that screens affect sleep.
Certeza media: parece, pero no está probado
It remains unclear whether the effect lasts.
Certeza baja: aún no hay respuesta
To a certain extent, the timetable explains the results.
Alcance limitado: solo una parte de la explicación

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha y elige qué critica exactamente el lector del informe.
evaluacion.feedback: El lector acepta los resultados del informe, pero critica que el titular sea más rotundo que lo que los datos permiten.
evaluacion.audio: The school's sleep report has been praised, but one reader wrote in with a criticism. According to his letter, the authors wrote in their headline that screens ruin sleep, yet their own findings section says something much weaker: it appears that screen use may be linked to shorter sleep, and it remains unclear whether the effect is large. The reader does not accuse the authors of lying. He simply thinks that a headline should match the evidence below it, and that a careful report would have said there is some evidence that screens affect sleep.
opciones: That the headline is stronger than the findings below it.
That the findings section contains figures that are wrong.
That the authors have hidden the size of the effect.

evaluacion.consigna: Con el mismo audio, elige cómo habría redactado el lector el titular.
evaluacion.feedback: El lector sugiere que un informe cuidadoso habría dicho there is some evidence that screens affect sleep.
evaluacion.audio: The school's sleep report has been praised, but one reader wrote in with a criticism. According to his letter, the authors wrote in their headline that screens ruin sleep, yet their own findings section says something much weaker: it appears that screen use may be linked to shorter sleep, and it remains unclear whether the effect is large. The reader does not accuse the authors of lying. He simply thinks that a headline should match the evidence below it, and that a careful report would have said there is some evidence that screens affect sleep.
opciones: With a cautious hedge, such as there is some evidence that.
With a stronger verb, since the data come from a survey.
With a question that lets readers decide for themselves.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «Los resultados dependen en gran medida de cómo respondió ese grupo.»
evaluacion.feedback: Largely indica que los resultados dependen, en su mayor parte, de las respuestas de un solo grupo pequeño.
evaluacion.texto: Nearly all the data come from one group of students, so the findings depend ___ on how that group answered. A wider study would be needed to confirm them.

evaluacion.consigna: Reescribe el hallazgo con «It appears that» y una cautela más.
evaluacion.feedback: It appears that… introduce el hallazgo con prudencia y la segunda cautela (tend to, it remains unclear whether, not conclusive) evita afirmar una causa.
evaluacion.texto: Hallazgo rotundo: «Students who eat breakfast get better grades.» Reescríbelo para un informe con It appears that… y una cautela adicional (tend to, it remains unclear whether…).
evaluacion.respuesta: It appears that students who eat breakfast tend to get better grades, although it remains unclear whether breakfast is the cause.
aceptadas: It appears that students who have breakfast may get better grades, but it is unclear whether breakfast explains the difference.
It appears that students who eat breakfast tend to get better grades, although the evidence is not conclusive.

repaso.consigna: Lee el párrafo y elige qué afirmación se formula con más certeza.
repaso.feedback: The data indicate… es la fórmula más firme del párrafo; it remains unclear y may marcan dudas sobre el efecto del horario.
opciones: Most students sleep too little, according to the data.
A later start would probably change how much students sleep.
The answer may depend on how students spend their evenings.
repaso.texto: Extract from a report: 'The data indicate that seventy percent of students sleep too little. It remains unclear whether a later start would change that, and to a certain extent the answer may depend on how students spend their evenings.'

repaso.consigna: Escucha y elige qué le pide la tutora a la estudiante.
repaso.feedback: La tutora propone sustituir proves por una fórmula prudente, porque los préstamos no demuestran que se lea más.
repaso.audio: My tutor returned my essay with a comment: you write that the new library proves that students read more. The figures only indicate a rise in loans, and it remains unclear whether people actually read the books. She suggested this instead: there is some evidence that loans have risen, which may reflect more reading.
opciones: To replace a firm claim with a more careful one.
To add more figures about the loans in the library.
To explain why the library has become so popular.

repaso.consigna: Completa: «La encuesta fue algo limitada, así que los resultados son provisionales.»
repaso.feedback: Somewhat suaviza la crítica: la encuesta tiene límites, pero no se descarta por completo.
repaso.texto: The survey was ___ limited, though not useless, so the authors describe their findings as tentative rather than final. They also say that more data are needed.

classes.objetivo: Clasificar enunciados de un informe como hecho, inferencia u opinión según su formulación y señalar la pista lingüística.

ensenanza.en: It is a fact that 62 percent of the students sleep less than eight hours, and the report names its source so that readers can check the figure.
ensenanza.es: Es un hecho que el 62 % de los estudiantes duerme menos de ocho horas, y el informe nombra su fuente para que los lectores puedan comprobar la cifra.
ensenanza.nota: Fact: algo que se puede comprobar, con cifras o fuente. En inglés es obligatorio el sujeto it en It is a fact that…

ensenanza.en: We can assume that the school cut homework, but that is an inference, not a fact, and we would need the school's records to confirm it.
ensenanza.es: Podemos suponer que el colegio redujo las tareas, pero eso es una inferencia, no un hecho, y necesitaríamos los registros del colegio para confirmarlo.
ensenanza.nota: Una inferencia se deduce de los hechos; assume y suggest son pistas de que no está comprobada.

ensenanza.en: Whether homework should be shorter is a matter of opinion, and unfortunately nobody asked the students what they think about it.
ensenanza.es: Si las tareas deberían ser más cortas es cuestión de opinión, y por desgracia nadie preguntó a los estudiantes qué piensan al respecto.
ensenanza.nota: A matter of opinion: no se puede comprobar. In my opinion, should y unfortunately son pistas de opinión: valoran en lugar de comprobar.

ensenanza.en: According to the school nurse, the source of the figure is a national survey, which is more reliable than second-hand stories from the corridor.
ensenanza.es: Según la enfermera del colegio, la fuente de la cifra es una encuesta nacional, que es más fiable que las historias de segunda mano del pasillo.
ensenanza.nota: According to + persona o documento atribuye el dato; second-hand describe información que llega a través de otros. No se dice «according to me».

ensenanza.en: Presumably, late screen use explains the drop, but that is speculation until someone tests it, so the certainty of the statement is low.
ensenanza.es: Presumiblemente, el uso de pantallas por la noche explica la caída, pero eso es especulación hasta que alguien lo compruebe, así que la certeza de la afirmación es baja.
ensenanza.nota: Presumably marca una inferencia: probable, no comprobada; speculation es una idea sin pruebas.

ensenanza.en: Reportedly, the school has cut homework by a third, although I cannot confirm it, and the evidence so far is only anecdotal and rather subjective.
ensenanza.es: Según se dice, el colegio ha reducido las tareas en un tercio, aunque no puedo confirmarlo, y las pruebas hasta ahora son solo anecdóticas y bastante subjetivas.
ensenanza.nota: Reportedly atribuye la información a otros sin confirmarla; anecdotal y subjective describen pruebas basadas en casos sueltos o en impresiones personales.

explicacion.texto: Un informe mezcla tres tipos de enunciados. Un hecho (fact) se puede comprobar y suele llevar cifras o fuente: According to the survey, 62 percent… Una inferencia es una conclusión deducida de los hechos y lleva matizadores: suggests, presumably, is likely to; sin comprobarla es speculation. Una opinión es una valoración personal y subjetiva (a matter of opinion): in my opinion, should, unfortunately, obviously. Reportedly atribuye un dato a otros sin confirmarlo, y las pruebas anecdotal o second-hand valen menos que una fuente clara. La pista está en las palabras: cifra + fuente = hecho; presumably = inferencia; should = opinión.

formula.texto: According to the survey, 62 percent…
Presumably, screens explain the drop.
In my opinion, schools should start later.
Reportedly, the school has cut homework.

filas.texto: cifras, fechas, According to…, It is a fact that…
suggests, presumably, is likely to, appears to
In my opinion, should, unfortunately, obviously

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: According to me, schools should start later.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: In my opinion, schools should start later.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Aunque en español se diga «según yo», en inglés se usa In my opinion; according to se reserva para atribuir un dato a otra persona o a un documento.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Is a fact that 62 percent sleep little.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: It is a fact that 62 percent sleep little.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: En inglés el sujeto no puede omitirse: hace falta it aunque en español se diga «es un hecho».

situacion.contexto: Mia y Leo analizan frases de un informe escolar para decidir cuáles son hechos y cuáles opiniones.

dialogo.texto: Look at this sentence: «Schools should start later.» Is it a fact?
dialogo.traduccion: Mira esta frase: «Los colegios deberían empezar más tarde». ¿Es un hecho?

dialogo.texto: No, it's an opinion. The word should gives it away.
dialogo.traduccion: No, es una opinión. La palabra should lo delata.

dialogo.texto: And this one: «According to the survey, 62 percent sleep less than eight hours.»
dialogo.traduccion: ¿Y esta otra: «Según la encuesta, el 62 % duerme menos de ocho horas»?

dialogo.texto: That's a fact, and it names the source.
dialogo.traduccion: Es un hecho y nombra la fuente.

dialogo.texto: What about: «Presumably, screens are the cause»?
dialogo.traduccion: ¿Y «Presumiblemente, las pantallas son la causa»?

dialogo.texto: That's an inference. Presumably shows it isn't certain.
dialogo.traduccion: Es una inferencia. Presumably muestra que no es seguro.

item.consigna: Según el diálogo, ¿qué pista indica que «Schools should start later» es una opinión?
item.feedback: Leo dice «The word should gives it away»: should marca una valoración, no algo comprobable.

guiada.consigna: Lee el extracto y elige cómo clasificar «Presumably, late screen use explains the drop».
guiada.feedback: Presumably presenta la explicación como probable pero sin comprobar: es una inferencia, no un hecho ni una opinión.
opciones: Inference: presumably marks a likely explanation that has not been tested.
Fact: the nurse states it, so it has been checked and confirmed.
Opinion: unfortunately shows that the writer is unhappy about it.
guiada.texto: Extract from the report: 'According to the school nurse, 62 percent of students sleep fewer than eight hours. Presumably, late screen use explains the drop, but no one has tested this idea. Unfortunately, the school has done nothing about it so far.'
guiada.pista: Busca la palabra que dice que algo es probable pero no está comprobado.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «Podemos suponer que redujeron las tareas, pero nadie lo ha probado.»
guiada.feedback: Assume (o presume) introduce una suposición; en un informe indica una inferencia que aún no está comprobada.
guiada.texto: The report says that homework is lighter this year. We can ___ that the school cut it, but nobody has proved this yet. That is an inference, not a fact.
guiada.pista: Es el verbo que introduce algo que damos por probable, sin pruebas.

guiada.consigna: Ordena: «Según la enfermera, la fuente de la cifra es una encuesta nacional.»
guiada.feedback: According to + persona atribuye el dato y source permite comprobarlo: es la estructura típica de un hecho.
guiada.respuesta: According to the nurse the source of the figure is a national survey
guiada.pista: Empieza por la fórmula que atribuye el dato a una persona.

practica.consigna: Escucha y elige qué frase de la lectura es una opinión y por qué.
practica.feedback: La profesora señala que excellent es una valoración personal: por eso esa frase es una opinión. La cifra tiene fuente y la subida de asistencia es una inferencia.
practica.audio: A teacher is reading a school report aloud and commenting on it. The report says that seventy percent of students prefer the new timetable. That is a fact, she says, because the figure comes from a named survey. Then it says that the new timetable is an excellent improvement. That, she explains, is an opinion, and the word excellent gives it away. Finally, the report says that presumably attendance will rise. That is an inference, because nobody has checked it yet.
opciones: That the timetable is an excellent improvement, because that word expresses a personal view.
That seventy percent prefer the new timetable, because the figure has no named source.
That attendance will rise, because the writer is completely sure about the result.

practica.consigna: Relaciona cada pista lingüística con el tipo de enunciado.
practica.feedback: Cada pista apunta a un tipo: fuente y cifra, probabilidad, valoración o información atribuida a otros.
pares: According to the survey, 62 percent…
Hecho: cifra con fuente
Presumably, screens explain the drop.
Inferencia: probable, no comprobada
Unfortunately, schools ignore sleep.
Opinión: valoración personal
Reportedly, homework was cut.
Sin confirmar: lo dicen otros

practica.consigna: Elige cómo clasificar el titular según el estudio que cita el artículo.
practica.feedback: El estudio mide una diferencia de 40 minutos, pero el titular la presenta como motivo: es una inferencia exagerada.
opciones: An overstated inference: the study shows a difference, not a reason.
A plain fact: the study has measured the forty minutes of lost sleep.
Simply an opinion, because the headline contains no figure at all.
practica.texto: Headline: 'Phones are the reason why teenagers sleep badly.' Below it, the article quotes one study: teenagers who use their phones at night sleep forty minutes less, on average, than those who do not.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha y elige qué hará la periodista con la frase sobre la cantina.
evaluacion.feedback: La periodista subraya la frase, la considera una inferencia y no la publicará hasta que el colegio aporte pruebas.
evaluacion.audio: A journalist is checking a school press release before publishing it. The release says that attendance has reached ninety-five percent, according to the school office. That is a fact that can be checked, she notes, and she will confirm it with the office. It then says that the new canteen is the reason for the improvement. She underlines that statement: it is an inference at best, because the release gives no evidence, and she will not print it until the school provides some. Finally, the release says that all the parents are happy. She crosses that out, since nobody has asked them: in her view it is only a guess presented as a fact.
opciones: Ask the school for evidence before she prints it.
Print it as a fact, since the school office said so.
Delete it, because it is only the opinion of the parents.

evaluacion.consigna: Con el mismo audio, elige por qué tacha la frase sobre los padres.
evaluacion.feedback: Nadie ha preguntado a los padres: la frase es una suposición que el comunicado presenta como si fuera un hecho.
evaluacion.audio: A journalist is checking a school press release before publishing it. The release says that attendance has reached ninety-five percent, according to the school office. That is a fact that can be checked, she notes, and she will confirm it with the office. It then says that the new canteen is the reason for the improvement. She underlines that statement: it is an inference at best, because the release gives no evidence, and she will not print it until the school provides some. Finally, the release says that all the parents are happy. She crosses that out, since nobody has asked them: in her view it is only a guess presented as a fact.
opciones: Because nobody asked the parents, so it is a guess.
Because the school office has already denied it publicly.
Because it is a fact, but one that the school office has not confirmed.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «Nadie ha comprobado esta idea, así que es pura especulación y no un hecho.»
evaluacion.feedback: Speculation es una idea sin pruebas; presentarla como un hecho confunde al lector.
evaluacion.texto: Nobody has tested this idea, so it is nothing more than ___ and should not be presented as a fact. A careful writer would label it as a guess.

evaluacion.consigna: Elige la opción que clasifica bien las tres frases del boletín.
evaluacion.feedback: A lleva cifra y fuente (hecho); B usa obviously y best (opinión); C usa presumably (inferencia).
opciones: A is a fact, B is an opinion, C is an inference.
A is an inference, B is a fact, C is an opinion.
A is an opinion, B is an inference, C is a fact.
evaluacion.texto: Statements from a town newsletter. A: 'The library has added 4,000 new members since January, according to the council.' B: 'The library is obviously the best place in town.' C: 'Presumably, the new café inside explains the rise.'

repaso.consigna: Lee la columna y elige qué da a entender el autor sobre la decisión del consejo.
repaso.feedback: Unfortunately y presumably muestran su opinión; además contrapone la versión de un padre a las cifras oficiales, que muestran una subida.
opciones: That the decision was taken without checking the facts, in his view.
That the decision is understandable, since a parent says that fewer children use the pool.
That the decision is only a rumour with no official record at all.
repaso.texto: Column: 'Unfortunately, the council has reportedly decided to close the pool. Presumably, nobody checked how many children use it. One parent said that attendance had fallen, although the council's own figures, published in March, show a rise.'

repaso.consigna: Escucha y elige cómo describe la amiga la frase sobre el laboratorio nuevo.
repaso.feedback: Reportedly atribuye la noticia a otros, y el autor admite que no la ha confirmado.
repaso.audio: Two friends are discussing an article. One says that it claims the school is the best in the region. The other says that this is only an opinion, because it does not say where the figures come from. She adds that the article also says, reportedly, that the school will open a new lab, but the writer admits that he has not confirmed it.
opciones: As information from others that the writer has not confirmed.
As a fact that the writer has checked with the school.
As a personal opinion that the writer has made up.

repaso.consigna: Completa: «Una afirmación sin fuente identificada es difícil de comprobar.»
repaso.feedback: Sin una fuente identificada, un dato no se puede verificar, por llamativo que sea.
repaso.texto: A claim without a named ___ is hard to check, so careful readers treat it with care. Even a striking number means little if nobody can say where it comes from.

classes.objetivo: Redactar los resultados de una encuesta escolar con conectores formales, cifras, una fuente y afirmaciones matizadas.

vocabulario.es: a la inversa, por el contrario

ensenanza.en: Furthermore, the percentage of students who sleep under seven hours rises in the final year, reaching seventy percent in some classes.
ensenanza.es: Además, el porcentaje de estudiantes que duerme menos de siete horas sube en el último curso, hasta llegar al setenta por ciento en algunas clases.
ensenanza.nota: Furthermore añade un dato en la misma línea y es más formal que and also; percentage es el porcentaje (sin the delante de la cifra).

ensenanza.en: Only a minority of respondents use a phone after midnight; nevertheless, they report the worst sleep, albeit in a very small group.
ensenanza.es: Solo una minoría de los encuestados usa el móvil después de medianoche; sin embargo, son los que dicen dormir peor, si bien en un grupo muy pequeño.
ensenanza.nota: Nevertheless contrasta con lo anterior: antes lleva punto y coma, y después, coma. Albeit introduce una salvedad (= although it is).

ensenanza.en: Most respondents said that they feel tired in the morning; therefore, the school may wish to review the timetable.
ensenanza.es: La mayoría de los encuestados dijo que se siente cansada por la mañana; por tanto, el colegio podría querer revisar el horario.
ensenanza.nota: Therefore introduce la consecuencia. Lleva punto y coma o punto delante, no una simple coma.

ensenanza.en: These results are consistent with the national survey, which stated that teenagers sleep too little, in terms of both hours and quality.
ensenanza.es: Estos resultados son coherentes con la encuesta nacional, que afirmó que los adolescentes duermen poco, tanto en horas como en calidad.
ensenanza.nota: Consistent with integra una fuente externa; stated introduce lo que dijo esa fuente (pasado); in terms of + sustantivo delimita el aspecto.

ensenanza.en: Notably, the biggest rise was among students in their final year; conversely, the youngest students reported no change at all.
ensenanza.es: En particular, el mayor aumento se dio entre los estudiantes del último curso; a la inversa, los más jóvenes no notificaron ningún cambio.
ensenanza.nota: Notably destaca un dato concreto dentro de los resultados; conversely presenta el caso opuesto.

ensenanza.en: All year groups showed the same pattern, with the exception of the first year, where the percentage of tired students fell slightly.
ensenanza.es: Todos los cursos mostraron el mismo patrón, con la excepción del primero, donde el porcentaje de estudiantes cansados bajó ligeramente.
ensenanza.nota: With the exception of + sustantivo señala el único caso que no sigue la regla.

explicacion.titulo: Escribir los resultados de una encuesta
explicacion.texto: Un apartado de resultados enlaza cifras con conectores formales: furthermore (añade), nevertheless o conversely (contrastan: «sin embargo», «a la inversa»), therefore (consecuencia). Cita las fuentes con according to…, the national survey stated that… o consistent with…, y matiza al menos dos afirmaciones con it appears that, may o tend to. Orden: dato, conector, interpretación prudente y fuente. Con porcentajes no se usa the: Forty percent of respondents… Para limitar un dato usa albeit, in terms of o with the exception of.

formula.texto: Sixty percent of respondents sleep under eight hours;
furthermore, the percentage is higher in the final year.
This may be linked to exams,
consistent with the national survey.

filas.texto: according to…, stated that…, consistent with…
it appears that, may, tend to

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: The sample is small, therefore the results are unclear.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: The sample is small; therefore, the results are unclear.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Therefore no puede unir dos oraciones con una coma sola: necesita punto y coma (o punto) delante y coma detrás.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: The 40 percent of respondents use a phone after midnight.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Forty percent of respondents use a phone after midnight.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: En una afirmación general, el porcentaje no lleva the delante de la cifra, aunque en español se diga «el 40 %».

situacion.contexto: Carlos y Ana redactan la sección de resultados de la encuesta del colegio sobre el sueño.

dialogo.texto: I've got the numbers: forty percent of respondents sleep under seven hours.
dialogo.traduccion: Ya tengo las cifras: el cuarenta por ciento de los encuestados duerme menos de siete horas.

dialogo.texto: Add a connector. Furthermore, the percentage is higher in the final year.
dialogo.traduccion: Añade un conector. Además, el porcentaje es más alto en el último curso.

dialogo.texto: And a contrast: a minority sleep well; nevertheless, they still feel tired.
dialogo.traduccion: Y un contraste: una minoría duerme bien; sin embargo, aun así se siente cansada.

dialogo.texto: Hmm, let's be more careful. It appears that exams may play a role.
dialogo.traduccion: Mmm, seamos más prudentes. Parece que los exámenes pueden influir.

dialogo.texto: And the source: consistent with the national survey.
dialogo.traduccion: Y la fuente: coherente con la encuesta nacional.

item.consigna: ¿Qué sugiere Ana para que el apartado de resultados sea más prudente?

opciones.es: Decir que los exámenes quizá influyen, con «may play a role».
Afirmar que los exámenes causan el problema, citando la encuesta nacional.
Añadir otro conector, como «furthermore», a cada frase.

item.feedback: Ana propone «It appears that exams may play a role»: dos matizadores (appears y may) en lugar de una causa afirmada.

guiada.consigna: Elige la frase formal que añade el segundo dato en el apartado de resultados.
guiada.feedback: Furthermore suma un dato en un registro formal; anyway es coloquial e in conclusion cierra el texto en lugar de añadir información.
opciones: Furthermore, the percentage is higher in the final year, reaching 70 percent.
Anyway, it's higher in the final year, like 70 percent or so.
In conclusion, the percentage is higher in the final year, reaching 70 percent.
guiada.texto: Data for the results section: 60 percent of the respondents sleep under eight hours. In the final year the figure is 70 percent. The writer wants a formal connector that adds the second fact to the first one.
guiada.pista: Busca el conector formal que suma un dato, no el que concluye ni el coloquial.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «Solo una minoría usa el móvil después de medianoche; sin embargo, duerme peor.»
guiada.feedback: Nevertheless contrasta dos datos: pocos usan el móvil, pero ese grupo duerme peor. Lleva punto y coma delante y coma detrás.
guiada.texto: Only a minority of respondents use a phone after midnight; ___, they report the worst sleep of the whole sample.
guiada.pista: Es el conector formal que significa «sin embargo» y va tras punto y coma.

guiada.consigna: Ordena: «Por tanto, el colegio podría plantearse un inicio más tardío.»
guiada.feedback: Therefore introduce la consecuencia del dato anterior; may wish to es una forma cortés y prudente de recomendar.
guiada.respuesta: Therefore the school may wish to consider a later start
guiada.pista: Empieza por el conector que introduce la consecuencia.

practica.consigna: Escucha el párrafo modelo y elige qué relación establece «nevertheless».
practica.feedback: Nevertheless une dos ideas que chocan: duermen bien y aun así se sienten cansados.
practica.audio: Listen to this model paragraph. The survey found that forty percent of respondents use a phone after midnight. Furthermore, the percentage is higher in the final year. Only a minority of students sleep well; nevertheless, they still report feeling tired. It appears that exams may play a role, which matches what the national survey found. Therefore, the school may wish to review its timetable.
opciones: It contrasts students who sleep well with their tiredness.
It adds one more reason why students sleep badly.
It draws a consequence from the previous figure.

practica.consigna: Relaciona cada conector con la función que cumple en un informe.
practica.feedback: Cada conector cumple un papel: sumar, contrastar, derivar una consecuencia o destacar un dato.
pares: Furthermore, the figure rises in year 11.
Añade un dato en la misma línea
Nevertheless, most students felt tired.
Contrasta con lo anterior
Therefore, the school may review its timetable.
Introduce una consecuencia
Notably, the highest figure is in year 11.
Destaca un dato concreto

practica.consigna: Completa: «Estos resultados son coherentes con la encuesta nacional.»
practica.feedback: Consistent with indica que los datos propios coinciden con los de otra fuente y refuerza los resultados.
practica.texto: Our school figure of 60 percent is very close to the national one. These results are ___ with the national survey, which stated that teenagers sleep too little.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha y elige qué le reprocha principalmente la profesora a la estudiante.
evaluacion.feedback: La profesora critica que la estudiante usa siempre and y but, de modo que no se ve cómo se relacionan las ideas.
evaluacion.audio: Your results section has good numbers, but the writing needs work. First, you use and and but for everything, so the reader cannot see how your ideas connect. A formal report would say furthermore to add a fact, nevertheless to contrast, and therefore to show a consequence. Second, you wrote that the national survey agrees with you, but you never named it, so I cannot check it. Finally, you say that phones cause tiredness. Your data show only a link, so it would be safer to say that it appears that phones may play a role.
opciones: That her writing does not show clearly how her ideas connect.
That her numbers are wrong and come from no named survey.
That she uses too many formal connectors in every single sentence.

evaluacion.consigna: Con el mismo audio, elige qué habría que cambiar en la frase sobre los móviles.
evaluacion.feedback: Los datos solo muestran un vínculo: la profesora propone sustituir la causa afirmada por it appears that… may play a role.
evaluacion.audio: Your results section has good numbers, but the writing needs work. First, you use and and but for everything, so the reader cannot see how your ideas connect. A formal report would say furthermore to add a fact, nevertheless to contrast, and therefore to show a consequence. Second, you wrote that the national survey agrees with you, but you never named it, so I cannot check it. Finally, you say that phones cause tiredness. Your data show only a link, so it would be safer to say that it appears that phones may play a role.
opciones: The claim of a cause should become a cautious statement about a link.
The figure for phones should be replaced with the national one instead.
The whole sentence should be moved to the method section of the report.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «En particular, el porcentaje más alto se da en el último curso.»
evaluacion.feedback: Notably destaca un dato concreto dentro de los resultados: aquí, el curso con el porcentaje más alto.
evaluacion.texto: Sleep problems are common in every year group. ___, the highest percentage is found in the final year, where it reaches seventy percent.

evaluacion.consigna: Escribe la sección de resultados con tres conectores, una fuente y dos matices.
evaluacion.feedback: La sección combina cifras, tres conectores formales, una fuente y al menos dos afirmaciones matizadas (it appears that, may, tend to).
evaluacion.texto: Encuesta escolar sobre el sueño (150 estudiantes): el 60 % duerme menos de ocho horas; en último curso, el 70 %; en primer curso, el 45 %; el 18 % usa el móvil después de medianoche y duerme peor. La encuesta nacional afirma que los adolescentes duermen poco. Escribe unas 125 a 200 palabras: tres conectores formales (furthermore, nevertheless, therefore…), la fuente y dos afirmaciones matizadas.
evaluacion.respuesta: The survey was completed by 150 students. The main findings show that 60 percent of respondents sleep fewer than eight hours. Furthermore, the percentage is higher in the final year, where it reaches 70 percent. Conversely, only 45 percent of first-year students sleep fewer than eight hours. Only a minority of students, 18 percent, use a phone after midnight; nevertheless, this group reports the worst sleep, albeit on a small sample. It appears that late phone use may be linked to poor sleep, although the survey cannot prove this. These results are consistent with the national survey, which stated that teenagers sleep too little. Therefore, the school may wish to consider a later start. Notably, the highest figure is found in the final year. More research is needed to confirm these findings.
aceptadas: According to the survey of 150 students, 60 percent sleep fewer than eight hours, and the figure rises to 70 percent in the final year. Moreover, only 45 percent of first-year students sleep so little. A minority of respondents, 18 percent, use a phone after midnight; however, they report the worst sleep, albeit in a small group. There is some evidence that phones may affect sleep, but the data do not show that they are the cause. The findings are consistent with the national survey, which stated that teenagers do not sleep enough. Therefore, it is recommended that the school should consider a later start. Notably, the figure is highest in the final year, and further research would be useful.

The survey of 150 students found that 60 percent sleep fewer than eight hours. In addition, the percentage rises to 70 percent in the final year, whereas it is 45 percent in the first year. A minority, 18 percent, use a phone after midnight; even so, these students report the worst sleep. It seems that late phone use may play a role, although the survey cannot prove it. According to the national survey, teenagers sleep too little, so the results are consistent with earlier research. As a result, the school may wish to consider a later start. Notably, the final year shows the highest figure, and more evidence would be welcome.

repaso.consigna: Elige la frase que integra la fuente nacional con prudencia.
repaso.feedback: Consistent with cita la fuente sin exagerar; proves y contradicts dicen más o algo distinto de lo que muestran las dos cifras.
opciones: Our figure of 60 percent is consistent with the national report, which stated that 55 percent sleep too little.
Our figure of 60 percent proves the national report, which is obviously right about teenagers everywhere.
Our figure of 60 percent contradicts the national report, although the two numbers are in fact very close.
repaso.texto: You must refer to a national report that found that 55 percent of teenagers sleep under eight hours. Your own school survey found 60 percent. The two figures are close, and your sample is much smaller than theirs.

repaso.consigna: Escucha y elige por qué prefiere Mia la segunda versión de la frase.
repaso.feedback: Mia prefiere la segunda porque refleja un vínculo, no una causa, y un informe no debe afirmar más de lo que permiten los datos.
repaso.audio: Mia is reading out two versions of a sentence. The first says that phones are the reason why students sleep badly. The second says that it appears that late phone use may be linked to poor sleep. She prefers the second one, because the survey shows a link and not a cause, and a good report should never claim more than the data allow.
opciones: Because it matches what the survey actually shows.
Because it is shorter and easier to read aloud.
Because it includes figures that the first one lacks.

repaso.consigna: Completa: «Solo una minoría de los encuestados usa el móvil después de medianoche.»
repaso.feedback: Minority significa menos de la mitad; combina con only para dejar claro que el grupo es pequeño.
repaso.texto: Only a ___ of respondents, about eighteen percent, use their phones after midnight, although that group reports the worst sleep.

classes.objetivo: Elaborar un mini informe sobre el transporte escolar y presentarlo en un resumen oral de un minuto con punto clave, cautela y recomendación.

ensenanza.en: In brief, this report gives an overview of how students make their daily commute to school, according to a survey of one hundred families.
ensenanza.es: En resumen, este informe ofrece una visión general de cómo hacen los estudiantes su trayecto diario al colegio, según una encuesta a cien familias.
ensenanza.nota: In brief resume en una frase; give an overview introduce el panorama general; commute es el trayecto diario al colegio o al trabajo.

ensenanza.en: I will outline the main findings in one minute, so I will pick out only the two or three figures that matter most to the listeners.
ensenanza.es: Presentaré a grandes rasgos los principales resultados en un minuto, así que seleccionaré solo las dos o tres cifras que más importan a los oyentes.
ensenanza.nota: I will outline… es la fórmula oral para anunciar el resumen; pick out es elegir lo más importante y dejar lo demás.

ensenanza.en: The key point is that most students depend on the school bus, and that is the key takeaway I want the audience to remember.
ensenanza.es: La idea clave es que la mayoría de los estudiantes depende del autobús escolar, y esa es la idea principal que quiero que recuerde el público.
ensenanza.nota: The key point is that… da la idea central; en una presentación oral se dice una sola vez y se repite al final como key takeaway.

ensenanza.en: To conclude, it appears that late buses are the main problem, although more evidence is needed before we can be certain.
ensenanza.es: Para concluir, parece que los autobuses con retraso son el problema principal, aunque hacen falta más pruebas antes de poder estar seguros.
ensenanza.nota: To conclude cierra el resumen; se mantiene la cautela de las clases anteriores (it appears, more evidence is needed).

ensenanza.en: We recommend a second morning bus, which would shorten the journey for the students who live furthest from the school.
ensenanza.es: Recomendamos un segundo autobús por la mañana, que acortaría el trayecto de los estudiantes que viven más lejos del colegio.
ensenanza.nota: We recommend + sustantivo o -ing; el condicional would dice el efecto esperado.

ensenanza.en: To keep the summary concise, I will mention only two findings and try to distil the report into one clear message, and I must keep to time.
ensenanza.es: Para que el resumen sea conciso, mencionaré solo dos resultados e intentaré condensar el informe en un mensaje claro, y debo ajustarme al tiempo.
ensenanza.nota: Un resumen oral breve elige los dos o tres datos más importantes; distil es condensar, y keep to time, no pasarse del tiempo.

explicacion.texto: El mini informe y el resumen oral comparten el esqueleto, pero no el estilo. Por escrito: secciones (aim, method, findings, conclusion), tono neutro y afirmaciones matizadas. Oralmente, en un minuto: anuncia (I will outline…), da el key point (The key point is that…) y elige (pick out) solo dos o tres cifras; añade una cautela (It appears that…, although more evidence is needed) y cierra con To conclude… y una recomendación. Las frases orales son más cortas, repiten la idea central y deben condensar (distil) el informe para ajustarse al tiempo (keep to time).

patron.texto: Visión general + punto clave + cautela + recomendación:

formula.texto: This report gives an overview of the school commute.
The key point is that most students use the bus.
It appears that journeys are long, although more evidence is needed.
To conclude, we recommend a second morning bus.

filas.texto: It appears that… although more evidence is needed

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: I will make a resume of the report.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: I will give a summary of the report.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Resume suena parecido a «resumen», pero significa currículum; el resumen es summary.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: We recommend to take a second bus.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: We recommend taking a second bus.
erroresFrecuentes.explicacion: Después de recommend se usa -ing o un sustantivo; no to + verbo.

situacion.contexto: Leo ensaya con Sara un resumen de un minuto sobre el informe del transporte escolar.

dialogo.texto: I have one minute. How should I start?
dialogo.traduccion: Tengo un minuto. ¿Cómo debería empezar?

dialogo.texto: Say: «I will outline the main findings of our report on the school commute.»
dialogo.traduccion: Di: «Esbozaré los principales resultados de nuestro informe sobre el trayecto al colegio».

dialogo.texto: Then the key point: most students arrive by bus, and the trip takes over forty minutes.
dialogo.traduccion: Luego el punto clave: la mayoría llega en autobús y el viaje dura más de cuarenta minutos.

dialogo.texto: Good. Now be careful: say it appears that late buses are the main problem.
dialogo.traduccion: Bien. Ahora sé prudente: di que parece que los autobuses tardíos son el problema principal.

dialogo.texto: And I finish with: «To conclude, we recommend a second morning bus.»
dialogo.traduccion: Y termino con: «Para concluir, recomendamos un segundo autobús por la mañana».

item.consigna: ¿Con qué debe cerrar Leo su resumen de un minuto?

opciones.es: Con una conclusión y una recomendación.
Con una pregunta abierta para el público.
Con la repetición de todas las cifras del informe.

item.feedback: Leo dice que termina con «To conclude, we recommend a second morning bus»: cierre con conclusión y recomendación.

guiada.consigna: Elige la frase que abre el informe con una visión general del tema.
guiada.feedback: Give an overview presenta el panorama general del tema y la base de datos; las otras opciones son una lista exhaustiva o una opinión personal.
opciones: This report gives an overview of how students travel to school, based on a survey of 100 students.
This report gives a long list of every answer that each student gave in the survey.
This report gives my own feelings about travelling to school with my friends every day.
guiada.texto: You surveyed 100 students about how they travel to school. Fifty-two come by school bus and thirty walk. Your report needs an opening sentence that gives the reader the overall picture, before any detail.
guiada.pista: Busca la frase que da el panorama general y cita la base de datos, sin opiniones ni listas.

guiada.consigna: Completa: «Para que el resumen sea conciso, mencionaré solo dos resultados.»
guiada.feedback: Concise describe un resumen breve y directo: solo lo esencial, sin repetir todo el informe.
guiada.texto: I have only one minute for the whole talk. To keep the summary ___, I will mention only two findings and leave the rest for the written report.
guiada.pista: Es el adjetivo que describe un texto breve que dice mucho con pocas palabras.

guiada.consigna: Ordena: «Recomendamos un segundo autobús por la mañana para los que viven lejos.»
guiada.feedback: We recommend + sustantivo dice qué propones; for students who live far away precisa a quién beneficia.
guiada.respuesta: We recommend a second morning bus for students who live far away
guiada.pista: Empieza por la fórmula que introduce la recomendación.

practica.consigna: Escucha y elige con qué idea cierra el resumen la oradora.
practica.feedback: La oradora cierra con To conclude, we recommend…: una propuesta que se deriva del problema principal.
practica.audio: Good morning. I will outline the main findings of our survey on school transport in one minute. The key point is that more than half of the students depend on the school bus. It appears that late buses are the main problem, although we need more evidence. To conclude, we recommend a second morning bus, which would shorten the trip for students who live far away.
opciones: With a proposal that follows from the problem she found.
With a warning that the evidence is too weak to justify any action.
With a summary of the two figures she has mentioned.

practica.consigna: Relaciona cada frase del resumen oral con su función.
practica.feedback: Un buen resumen oral anuncia, da la idea central, matiza y cierra con una recomendación.
pares: I will outline the main findings.
Anunciar el resumen
The key point is that most use the bus.
Dar la idea central
It appears that late buses are the problem.
Añadir una cautela
To conclude, we recommend a second bus.
Cerrar con una recomendación

practica.consigna: Elige la primera frase adecuada para un resumen oral de un minuto.
practica.feedback: En un resumen oral la primera frase es corta y anuncia el plan; la opción larga es de estilo escrito y la vaga no anuncia nada.
opciones: I will outline our main findings in one minute.
This report, which is based on a survey carried out among students of several year groups, will now be described in full detail.
Well, there is quite a lot of stuff that we could talk about, really.
practica.texto: Here are three options for the first sentence of a one-minute talk. You have very little time, so the opening sentence must be short, clear and useful.

evaluacion.consigna: Escucha y elige qué debe hacer el estudiante para mejorar su resumen.
evaluacion.feedback: La profesora pide elegir dos cifras y sustituir la certeza sobre la causa por it appears that…
evaluacion.audio: Your summary was clear, but it ran for almost two minutes, so you must cut it. You announced the topic well, and your key point about the school bus was memorable. However, you read out five different figures, and the audience will remember only one or two of them. Choose the two that matter most. You also sounded certain that late buses are the cause; say instead that it appears they may be the main problem. Finish with your recommendation, as you did, because it is the part that people act on.
opciones: Keep fewer figures and sound more careful about the cause.
Add more figures so that the audience trusts the results.
Move the recommendation to the start of the summary.

evaluacion.consigna: Con el mismo audio, elige qué valora positivamente la profesora.
evaluacion.feedback: La profesora alaba el anuncio claro del tema y el cierre con la recomendación, que es lo que el público puede aplicar.
evaluacion.audio: Your summary was clear, but it ran for almost two minutes, so you must cut it. You announced the topic well, and your key point about the school bus was memorable. However, you read out five different figures, and the audience will remember only one or two of them. Choose the two that matter most. You also sounded certain that late buses are the cause; say instead that it appears they may be the main problem. Finish with your recommendation, as you did, because it is the part that people act on.
opciones: The announcement of the topic and the final recommendation.
The large number of figures that were included in it.
The certain tone used to describe the main cause.

evaluacion.consigna: Completa: «En el próximo minuto presentaré brevemente los principales resultados.»
evaluacion.feedback: I will outline… es la fórmula habitual para anunciar un resumen breve de los resultados.
evaluacion.texto: Thank you all for coming. In the next minute I will briefly ___ the main findings of our survey on the commute, starting with the key point.

evaluacion.consigna: Escribe el mini informe: objetivo, método, resultados, matiz, conclusión y recomendación.
evaluacion.feedback: El mini informe lleva el objetivo, los resultados con cifras, una afirmación matizada, la conclusión y una recomendación, con tono neutro.
evaluacion.texto: Encuesta del consejo escolar a 100 estudiantes sobre cómo llegan al colegio: 52 en autobús escolar, 30 a pie, 12 en coche y 6 en bicicleta. El viaje en autobús dura más de 40 minutos para 35 estudiantes. Escribe unas 140 a 220 palabras: objetivo, método, resultados con cifras, una afirmación matizada, la conclusión y una recomendación, con tono neutro.
evaluacion.respuesta: The aim of this report is to describe how students travel to school. The method was a survey of 100 students carried out by the school council, and every answer was included in the analysis. The main findings show that 52 percent of respondents come by school bus, whereas only 6 percent cycle. The remaining students either walk, 30 percent, or come by car, 12 percent. Furthermore, 35 students said that the bus journey takes more than forty minutes. It appears that long journeys may be a problem for students who live far away, although more evidence is needed. The conclusion is that the school bus is the most common way to travel. Therefore, it is recommended that the school should consider a second morning bus, which would probably shorten the daily commute. The survey was somewhat limited, so the results should be treated as tentative.
aceptadas: This report gives an overview of how students get to school. A survey of 100 students was carried out by the school council. The findings show that more than half of the respondents, 52 percent, use the school bus, while 30 percent walk, 12 percent come by car and only 6 percent cycle. In addition, 35 students said that the journey by bus takes longer than forty minutes. There is some evidence that long journeys may affect students who live far away, but it remains unclear how many are affected. To conclude, the bus is the main way to travel. We recommend that the school consider an extra bus in the morning, which would shorten the daily commute for many families.

The aim of this report is to show how students travel to school. We surveyed 100 students, and every student answered in class, so all the replies could be included. According to the survey, 52 percent travel by school bus, 30 percent walk, 12 percent come by car and 6 percent cycle. Nevertheless, the bus is not always convenient: 35 students said that the journey takes over forty minutes. It seems that this may be a problem for those who live far away, although the survey cannot prove it. Therefore, we recommend a second morning bus. The conclusion is that the school bus is essential, and a second one could improve the daily commute for many students.

repaso.consigna: Lee el borrador y elige qué debería mejorar el resumen oral.
repaso.feedback: El borrador enumera cinco cifras seguidas sin decir cuál importa: falta una idea clave que el público pueda recordar.
opciones: It lists too many figures and lacks a clear key point.
It sounds too informal and includes too many personal opinions.
It should have started with the recommendation instead of the figures.
repaso.texto: Draft of a one-minute summary: 'Our survey asked 100 students about transport. We found that 52 came by bus, 30 walked, 12 came by car and 6 cycled. Also 35 said that the bus takes more than forty minutes, 22 said that it is sometimes late and 14 said that it is crowded.'

repaso.consigna: Escucha y elige por qué repetirá la estudiante la idea clave al final.
repaso.feedback: Al no poder releer, el oyente necesita que la idea central se repita al final.
repaso.audio: A student is comparing her written report with her oral summary. The report has a method section and a long list of findings. In the talk she will skip the method and mention only two findings, because the listeners cannot read the tables. She will repeat the key point at the end, so nobody forgets it.
opciones: Because listeners cannot go back and read it again.
Because the written report did not include that point.
Because she has to fill the whole minute with something.

repaso.consigna: Escribe el resumen oral de un minuto con anuncio, punto clave, cautela y recomendación.
repaso.feedback: El resumen anuncia, da el punto clave con una cifra, añade una cautela y cierra con una recomendación, en frases cortas.
repaso.texto: Encuesta sobre hábitos digitales (80 estudiantes): 64 usan el móvil más de tres horas al día; solo 20 duermen menos de siete horas; los que más lo usan parecen dormir menos. Escribe el resumen oral de un minuto (50 a 110 palabras): anuncio, punto clave con cifra, cautela y recomendación.
repaso.respuesta: I will outline the main findings of our survey on digital habits. The key point is that 64 of the 80 students use a phone for more than three hours a day. Only a minority, 20 students, sleep fewer than seven hours. It appears that heavy users tend to sleep less, although more evidence is needed. To conclude, we recommend a phone-free hour before bed.
aceptadas: I will briefly present our survey on digital habits. The main point is that most students, 64 out of 80, use a phone for more than three hours daily. It seems that heavy users may sleep less, but we cannot be sure. Only 20 students sleep fewer than seven hours. In conclusion, we recommend one hour without phones before bed.

I will give an overview of our digital habits survey. The key finding is that 64 of our 80 students use a phone for over three hours a day. It appears that heavy users tend to sleep less, although more evidence is needed. In short, we recommend a phone-free hour before bed.

notes: Claves verificadas en las 5 clases; distractores reescritos como casi-aciertos (registro, atribución, postura invertida) en al menos la mitad de los elegir/escuchar.

Enseñanza/explicación sin la frase clave de ítems de evaluación: C36 RE completar (summary) y C37 EV completar (largely) y C37 RE (somewhat) rehechos o con enseñanza ajustada; C40 PR elegir ya no revela la clave de RE escuchar.

C40 RE elegir: opción 'demasiado corto' era defendible y se sustituyó; C37 RE completar acotado para que 'very' no sea válido; aceptadas ampliadas (goal, people/pupils, infer/guess, fraction/fifth, nonetheless, summarize/describe/cover…).
Español neutro: 'deberes' -> 'tareas' (C38), 'Vale' eliminado; explicación de C33 y C40 sin inglés incrustado en frases españolas.

Vocabulario añadido verificado como colocaciones C1 (carry out, set out, to a certain extent, call into question, a degree of, matter of opinion, with the exception of, in terms of, key takeaway, distil, pick out, keep to time).
